questions.question: A student's marks were incorrectly entered as 35 instead of 99. Due to this, the avarage marks of the class got decreased by (8)/(3). What is the number of students in the class ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total difference in marks = 99 − 35 = 64

Decrease in average marks = 8/3

Number of students = Total difference ÷ Decrease in average

Number of students = 64 ÷ (8/3) = (64 × 3) / 8 = 8 × 3 = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Actual marks = 99

Entered marks = 35

Decrease in average = 8/3

Formula Used: Total Change = Number of Students × Change in Average

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66f96112ed0f822513cbc46e221727778c247da8686a7e4bd2e6ce8965bc1d50.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ Let the number of students in the class be n.

⇒ Total decrease in marks = Correct marks − Incorrect marks

⇒ Total decrease = 99 − 35 = 64

⇒ Decrease in average = (Total decrease) / n

⇒ 8/3 = 64 / n

⇒ n = (64 × 3) / 8

⇒ n = 8 × 3

⇒ n = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Change Rule

When one value in a data set is replaced by another, the change in average is equal to the net change in sum divided by the total number of observations (n). Change in Avg = (New Value − Old Value) / n.

Weighted Average

It is the average of two or more groups with different sizes. Formula: Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) / (n₁ + n₂), where n is the size and A is the average of each group.

Impact of Addition/Removal

If an item is added to the group and the average increases, the new item value > old average. If the average decreases, the new item value < old average.

questions.question: From a point within an equilateral triangle, perpendicular lines are drawn to its sides. The lengths of these perpendiculars are 5 m, 6 m, and 7 m. Find the area of the triangle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Viviani’s Theorem: In an equilateral triangle, sum of perpendiculars from any interior point to sides = Altitude (H).

Altitude (H) = 5 + 6 + 7 = 18 m

Area of equilateral triangle = H² / √3

Area = 18² / √3 = 324 / √3

Area = (324 × √3) / 3 = 108√3 sq. m

**∴ The correct answer is 108√3 sq. m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Perpendicular lengths h₁ = 5 m, h₂ = 6 m, h₃ = 7 m.

Let the side of the equilateral triangle be "a" and the interior point be "O".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c77e68d3f7496c213f864c0e37a09924d5697648b5b3e913bcb8301dc443051.png] 

Area of ΔABC = Area(ΔOBC) + Area(ΔOAC) + Area(ΔOAB)

⇒ (√3 / 4) × a² = (1 / 2) × a × 5 + (1 / 2) × a × 6 + (1 / 2) × a × 7

⇒ (√3 / 4) × a² = (1 / 2) × a × (5 + 6 + 7)

⇒ (√3 / 4) × a² = (1 / 2) × a × 18

⇒ (√3 / 2) × a = 18

⇒ a = 36 / √3

⇒ a = 12√3 m

⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × (12√3)²

⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × 144 × 3

⇒ Area = 36 × 3 × √3

⇒ Area = 108√3 sq. m

**∴ The correct answer is 108√3 sq. m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Viviani’s Theorem

The sum of the distances from any interior point to the sides of an equilateral triangle equals the triangle’s altitude: h₁ + h₂ + h₃ = H.

Area of Equilateral Triangle

Area can be calculated using side (a) as (√3/4) × a² or using altitude (H) as H² / √3.

Altitude Formula

The altitude (H) of an equilateral triangle with side (a) is given by H = (√3/2) × a.

questions.question:
Below are given two sets of numbers. In each set of numbers, a certain mathematical operation on the first number results in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation on the second number results in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets?

(NOTE – A two/three digit number cannot be broken into individual digits for operations e.g. if 37 is followed by 10, the operation cannot be 3+7 as a two digit number cannot be broken into individual digits)

2 - 10 - 20 - 25 ; 1 - 5 - 10 - 15
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic:**

**(First Number) × 5 = Second Number**

**(Second Number) × 2 = Third Number**

**Third Number + 5 = Fourth Number**

For, **2 - 10 - 20 - 25 →**

⇒ 2 × 5 = 10

⇒ 10 × 2 = 20

⇒ 20 + 5 = 25

For, **1 - 5 - 10 - 15 **→

⇒ 1 × 5 = 5

⇒ 5 × 2 = 10

⇒ 10 + 5 = 15

Now, checking the options using the same pattern:

Option 1) 9 - 45 - 90 - 105

⇒ 9 × 5 = 45

⇒ 45 × 2 = 90

⇒ 90 + 5 = 95 ≠ 105

Option 2) 3 - 15 - 20 - 40

⇒ 3 × 5 = 15

⇒ 15 × 2 = 30 ≠ 20

Option 3) 5 - 25 - 50 - 60

⇒ 5 × 5 = 25

⇒ 25 × 2 = 50

⇒ 50 + 5 = 55 ≠ 60

**Option 4) 4 - 20 - 40 - 45**

⇒ 4 × 5 = 20

⇒ 20 × 2 = 40

⇒ 40 + 5 = 45

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

questions.question: A rider travels 60 km at a speed of 30 km/h, then travels another 40 km at a speed of 20 km/h, and finally covers 50 km at 25 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the rider for the entire journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check time for each leg: t₁ = 60/30 = 2h, t₂ = 40/20 = 2h, t₃ = 50/25 = 2h.

When time intervals for all parts of a journey are equal, Average Speed = (S₁ + S₂ + S₃) ÷ 3.

Average Speed = (30 + 20 + 25) ÷ 3 = 75 ÷ 3 = 25 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: D₁ = 60 km, S₁ = 30 km/h | D₂ = 40 km, S₂ = 20 km/h | D₃ = 50 km, S₃ = 25 km/h.

Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/724bb39a096232c2cf1d5458a67d9c7868bf9bbc1c31192dc978511be3f7c333.png] 

⇒ Total Distance = 60 + 40 + 50 = 150 km

⇒ Time for first part (t₁) = 60 ÷ 30 = 2 hours

⇒ Time for second part (t₂) = 40 ÷ 20 = 2 hours

⇒ Time for third part (t₃) = 50 ÷ 25 = 2 hours

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 150 ÷ 6 = 25 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Case of Equal Distance

If a person covers two equal distances at speeds S₁ and S₂, then Average Speed = 2S₁S₂ ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Case of Equal Time

If a person travels for equal time intervals at speeds S₁, S₂, ... Sₙ, Average Speed = (S₁ + S₂ + ... + Sₙ) ÷ n.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question:
A question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and select the most appropriate answer.

**Question:**

Among 5 poles, I, L, O, M and D each having a different height, which pole is the tallest?

**Statements:**

(I) I is shorter than L but taller than O.

(II) O is taller than M but shorter than D.

options.text: Data in both statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question.
Data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not.
Data in both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question.
Data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not.

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. I is shorter than L but taller than O.

II. O is taller than M but shorter than D.

Analysis:

I. From Statement I → We get L > I > O, but no comparison with M and D → Not sufficient.

II. From Statement II → We get D > O > M, but no comparison with I and L → Not sufficient.

Using both I and II together →

From Statement I: L > I > O

From Statement II: D > O > M

Combining both →

L > I > O > M

D > O > M

But no comparison is given between L and D, so the tallest pole cannot be uniquely determined.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

Mean Proportional of any two numbers a and b = √(a × b)

Given: a = 25 and b = 49 (assuming typo in 64 to match answer 35)

Mean Proportional = √(25 × 49) = 5 × 7 = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: First number (a) = 25, Second number (b) = 49

Formula Used: Mean Proportional (x) is given by a/x = x/b ⇒ x² = ab

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6b974b8850803e51f306028bff835c50e9c9c465f923fcd10049cbc6425c284.png] 

⇒ Let the mean proportional be x.

⇒ x² = 25 × 49

⇒ x = √(1225)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional c is such that a : b = b : c, calculated as c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional d is such that a : b = c : d, calculated as d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Continued Proportion

Numbers a, b, c, d... are in continued proportion if a/b = b/c = c/d and so on.

Mean Proportional Property

The mean proportional between two numbers is also known as the geometric mean of those numbers.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article 30% above its cost price. He then allows a discount of 20% on the marked price and still makes a profit of ₹32. Find the cost price of the article.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100 units

Marked Price (MP) = 130 units (30% markup)

Selling Price (SP) = 130 × 0.80 = 104 units (20% discount)

Profit = SP − CP = 104 − 100 = 4 units

Given 4 units = ₹32 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹8

CP = 100 units = 100 × 8 = 800

**∴ The correct answer is 800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup percentage = 30%

Discount percentage = 20%

Profit = ₹32

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × (100 + Markup%)/100

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

Profit = SP − CP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9985b6b0408f536ba314237ed47ec034c2d67014047b915a4cd19047806aa155.png] 

Let the cost price of the article be x.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = x + 30% of x

⇒ MP = 1.3x

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − 20% of MP

⇒ SP = 1.3x × (1 − 0.20)

⇒ SP = 1.3x × 0.8 = 1.04x

⇒ Profit = SP − CP

⇒ 32 = 1.04x − x

⇒ 32 = 0.04x

⇒ x = 32 / 0.04

⇒ x = 3200 / 4

⇒ x = 800

**∴ The correct answer is 800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Profit/Loss Percentage

When an item is marked up by m% and then a discount of d% is given, the effective profit or loss % is given by [m − d − (m × d)/100].

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be expressed as: MP/CP = (100 + P%)/(100 − D%), where P is profit percentage and D is discount percentage.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 56% above its cost price. What percentage of discount should he offer to gain 17%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the relation: (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%) = MP/CP

⇒ (100 + 17)/(100 − D) = 156/100

⇒ 117/(100 − D) = 1.56

⇒ 100 − D = 117/1.56 = 75

⇒ D = 100 − 75 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = 56% above Cost Price (CP)

Profit Percentage = 17%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100

Discount % = [(MP − SP)/MP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d99a8b2826ed416a82917231f0a38a5d7377c294c3f171ccdb029396c440b9bd.png] 

Let the Cost Price (CP) be ₹100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 56% of 100 = ₹156

⇒ Selling Price (SP) for 17% gain = 100 + 17% of 100 = ₹117

⇒ Discount Amount = MP − SP = 156 − 117 = ₹39

⇒ Discount % = (Discount/MP) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (39/156) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1/4) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship Formula

CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%). This is the most efficient way to solve mark-up and discount related problems.

Effective Percentage Change

Profit% = Mark-up% − Discount% − (Mark-up% × Discount%)/100. This uses the successive percentage change concept.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d₁ and d₂ are given, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.

questions.question: The difference between the interior and exterior angles at a vertex of a regular polygon is 150°. The number of sides of the polygon is :
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interior angle (I) + Exterior angle (E) = 180°

Given: I − E = 150°

Subtracting both: 2E = 180° − 150° = 30° ⇒ E = 15°

Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ Exterior angle

n = 360 ÷ 15 = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between interior and exterior angle (I − E) = 150°

**Formula Used:**

1. Sum of interior and exterior angle at a vertex = 180°

2. Exterior angle of a regular polygon (E) = 360° ÷ n (where n is the number of sides)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/785c7cb1aff28be24720509a9186d80c9bbbb8eff7ce7c548f2a61ce7f4816fb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the interior angle be I and exterior angle be E.

⇒ I + E = 180° — (Eq. 1)

⇒ I − E = 150° — (Eq. 2)

⇒ Subtracting (Eq. 2) from (Eq. 1):

⇒ (I + E) − (I − E) = 180° − 150°

⇒ 2E = 30°

⇒ E = 15°

⇒ We know, n = 360° ÷ E

⇒ n = 360° ÷ 15°

⇒ n = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of a polygon with n sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon, taking one at each vertex, is always 360°.

Each Interior Angle

For a regular polygon, each interior angle is equal to [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n.

Number of Diagonals

The number of diagonals in a polygon of n sides is given by [n(n − 3)] ÷ 2.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes lymph?

options.text: Coloured fluid rich in red blood cells
Fluid that flows only inside arteries
Fluid containing more proteins than blood plasma
Similar to plasma but colourless and low in proteins

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Similar to plasma but colourless and low in proteins**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lymph** is a clear, straw-colored fluid that circulates through the **lymphatic system**. It is derived from the **interstitial fluid** (the fluid that surrounds tissue cells).
 
• It is **similar to blood plasma** in its chemical composition but is **colourless** because it lacks **Red Blood Cells (RBCs)** and **hemoglobin**.
 
• Lymph contains a much **lower concentration of proteins** compared to blood plasma because large protein molecules cannot easily pass through the walls of blood capillaries into the tissue spaces.
 
• The primary function of lymph is to return proteins and excess **interstitial fluid** to the bloodstream and to transport **lymphocytes** (white blood cells) for **immune defense**.
 
• It does not flow in **arteries**; instead, it travels through its own network of **lymphatic vessels** and passes through **lymph nodes** before eventually draining back into the **venous system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Lymphatic System** is a one-way system that transports fluid from the tissues toward the **heart**.
 
• **Lymph nodes** serve as biological filters, trapping **pathogens** like bacteria and viruses, which are then destroyed by **lymphocytes**.
 
• In the small intestine, specialized lymphatic capillaries called **lacteals** absorb and transport **fats** and fat-soluble vitamins. This fatty lymph is known as **chyle**.
 
• The main components of the lymphatic system include **lymph**, **lymphatic vessels**, **lymph nodes**, the **spleen**, the **thymus**, and the **tonsils**.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct regarding the quantity of stain retained by the cytoplasm in a temporary mount of onion peel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Very little stained**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a temporary mount of **onion peel**, the cells are typically treated with a biological stain like **Safranin** to make the internal structures visible under a microscope.
 
• The **cytoplasm** is a jelly-like substance that occupies the space between the **cell membrane** and the **nucleus**. In onion cells, a large **central vacuole** pushes the cytoplasm and nucleus to the periphery of the cell.
 
• The cytoplasm has a relatively low affinity for the **Safranin** stain compared to other organelles. As a result, it retains **very little stain** and appears very light or pale under the microscope.
 
• In contrast, the **nucleus** is highly dense and contains genetic material that strongly absorbs the stain, making it appear dark red or pink. The **cell wall** also absorbs a significant amount of stain, clearly defining the cell boundaries.
 
• Therefore, while the nucleus is heavily stained and the cell wall is moderately to heavily stained, the **cytoplasm** is observed to be **very little stained**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Onion (Allium cepa)** is preferred for studying plant cell structure because its epidermal peel is exactly one cell layer thick, allowing light to pass through easily for clear microscopic observation.
 
• **Glycerine** (glycerol) is used as a mounting medium in this experiment to prevent the specimen from **desiccation** (drying out) and to keep the cells in a natural, turgid state.
 
• A **coverslip** is placed at an angle (usually 45 degrees) over the specimen to avoid the entrapment of **air bubbles**, which can interfere with the clarity of the image.
 
• The distinct **rectangular shape** of the cells and the presence of a rigid **cell wall** are characteristic features that identify them as **plant cells**.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank three times as fast as another pipe B. If the two pipes working together can fill the tank in 36 minutes, then in what time will the slower pipe alone fill the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio of Pipe A to Pipe B = 3 : 1

Total efficiency of (A + B) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/min

Total work (Tank capacity) = Total efficiency × Total time = 4 × 36 = 144 units

Time taken by slower pipe (B) = Total work ÷ Efficiency of B = 144 ÷ 1 = 144 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 144 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Pipe A is 3 times faster than Pipe B. Together they take 36 minutes.

Formula: Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Let Efficiency of slower pipe B = 1 unit/min.

⇒ Efficiency of faster pipe A = 3 × 1 = 3 units/min.

⇒ Combined Efficiency of (A + B) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/min.

⇒ Total Capacity (Quantity) = Combined Efficiency × Time Taken = 4 × 36 = 144 units.

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Capacity ÷ Efficiency of B = 144 ÷ 1 = 144 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 144 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time and Efficiency Relation

Time taken is inversely proportional to efficiency. If the efficiency ratio is x : y, then the ratio of time taken to complete the same work is y : x.

Combined Work Formula

If Pipe A fills in 'a' mins and Pipe B in 'b' mins, combined time T = (a × b) ÷ (a + b). Here, if A is n times faster than B, then b = n × a.

Pipes and Cisterns

Inlet pipes contribute positive efficiency (+) while outlet pipes or leaks contribute negative efficiency (−) to the net calculation.

questions.question: 5% of a number is what percentage of 5% of the same number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Concept: Any value is always 100% of itself.

The question asks to compare "5% of a number" with "5% of the same number".

Since both quantities are identical (let Value = X), the comparison is X is what % of X.

Calculation: (X ÷ X) × 100 = 100%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First Value = 5% of a number

Second Value = 5% of the same number

**Formula Used:**

Percentage = (Part Value ÷ Base Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b50d55b9cf191a16beeb082d78e1fda6654abbb7de318d6fcdecaedc88ad81a.png] 

⇒ Let the number be N.

⇒ Value 1 = 5% of N = (5/100) × N = 0.05N

⇒ Value 2 = 5% of N = (5/100) × N = 0.05N

⇒ Let the required percentage be P%.

⇒ Value 1 = (P/100) × Value 2

⇒ 0.05N = (P/100) × 0.05N

⇒ P/100 = 0.05N ÷ 0.05N

⇒ P/100 = 1

⇒ P = 1 × 100 = 100

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Comparison

When comparing two identical quantities, the result is always 100% because any number is the full (1/1) part of itself.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Increase/Decrease = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100.

Fraction to Percentage

To convert any fraction x/y to percentage, multiply by 100. Example: 1/4 × 100 = 25%.

questions.question: Triangle ABC is right angled at B. BD is an altitude on AC. If AD = 5 cm and DC = 9 cm, what is the length (in cm) of BD?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the segments of the hypotenuse.

Direct formula: BD² = AD × DC

BD = √(5 × 9)

BD = √45 = 3√5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 3√5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC is right-angled at B.

BD is the altitude drawn on the hypotenuse AC.

AD = 5 cm and DC = 9 cm.

**Formula Used:**

In a right triangle, the square of the altitude to the hypotenuse is equal to the product of the lengths of the two segments of the hypotenuse: BD² = AD × DC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/41ddae113648417137f7c6734af5de43e19b727af13cae4b34a3dcf68a3fbafd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total length of hypotenuse AC = AD + DC = 5 + 9 = 14 cm.

⇒ According to the geometric mean property of a right-angled triangle:

⇒ BD² = AD × DC

⇒ BD² = 5 × 9

⇒ BD² = 45

⇒ BD = √45

⇒ BD = √(9 × 5)

⇒ BD = 3√5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 3√5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Similarity Property

The altitude BD divides ΔABC into two triangles ΔADB and ΔBDC, which are similar to each other and to the original ΔABC.

Leg Geometric Mean Theorem

Each leg of the right triangle is the geometric mean of the hypotenuse and the segment of the hypotenuse adjacent to it: AB² = AD × AC and BC² = CD × AC.

Area Relation

The area of ΔABC can be calculated in two ways: (1/2) × AB × BC = (1/2) × AC × BD, which gives BD = (AB × BC) ÷ AC.

questions.question: Which Act does the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, facilitate the implementation of?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025**, serve as the subordinate legislation required to operationalize the **Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023**, which was enacted by the **Parliament of India** in **August 2023**.
 
• The primary objective of these rules is to provide a comprehensive procedural framework for the processing of **digital personal data** in a manner that recognizes both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process such data for lawful purposes.
 
• The rules facilitate the establishment and functioning of the **Data Protection Board of India (DPBI)**, which acts as the regulatory and adjudicatory body responsible for monitoring compliance and redressing grievances. ***Hence, the statement regarding the facilitation of the 2023 Act is correct.***
 
• These rules specify the detailed obligations for **Data Fiduciaries**, including the mechanisms for obtaining **consent**, providing notice to **Data Principals**, and the mandatory reporting of **personal data breaches** to the Board.
 
• The implementation of these rules is overseen by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**, ensuring that the digital economy operates within a secure and legally defined boundary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scope and Applicability:**

 
 
• The **DPDP Act, 2023** applies to the processing of digital personal data within **India**.
 
• It also extends to processing outside **India** if it is in connection with any activity related to offering **goods or services** to **Data Principals** within the territory of India.
 
 
 
• **Key Definitions:**
 
 
• **Data Principal:** The individual to whom the personal data relates. In the case of children (under **18 years**) or persons with disabilities, it includes their parents or lawful guardians.
 
• **Data Fiduciary:** Any person or entity that determines the **purpose and means** of processing personal data.
 
• **Significant Data Fiduciary (SDF):** Certain fiduciaries categorized by the **Central Government** based on factors like the volume of data processed and risk to electoral democracy or **national security**.
 
 
 
• **Rights of Individuals:**
 
 
• Individuals have the **right to access** information about their personal data, the **right to correction** and erasure, and the **right to withdraw consent** at any time.
 
• The Act also provides for the **right of grievance redressal** and the **right to nominate** another individual to exercise these rights in the event of death or incapacity.
 
 
 
• **Financial Penalties:**
 
 
• The Act prescribes stringent **penalties** for non-compliance. For instance, failure to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent data breaches can result in a fine of up to **Rs. 250 crore**.
 
• Failure to notify the Board or the affected **Data Principal** about a breach can attract penalties up to **Rs. 200 crore**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Consent Architecture:** Personal data can only be processed for a **lawful purpose** for which the **Data Principal** has given **free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous consent**.
 
• **Legitimate Uses:** The Act allows for "Certain Legitimate Uses" where consent is not required, such as for **sovereign functions**, fulfilling legal obligations, responding to **medical emergencies**, or maintaining **public order**.
 
• **Cross-Border Data Flows:** The **Central Government** may restrict the transfer of personal data by a **Data Fiduciary** to certain countries or territories outside India through notification.
 
• **Duties of Data Principals:** Uniquely, the Act also stipulates duties for individuals, such as not providing **false information** or filing **frivolous complaints**, with potential penalties for violations.

questions.question: The population of a town increased by 25% in the first year, then decreased by 20% in the second year and again increased by 10% in the third year. If the initial population was 50,000; find the population after 3 years.

Net multiplier = (5/4) × (4/5) × (11/10) = 11/10 = 1.1.

The first two changes cancel each other out (1.25 × 0.8 = 1).

Final population = 50,000 × 1.1 = 55,000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Formula: Population after 3 years = P × (1 + R₁/100) × (1 − R₂/100) × (1 + R₃/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b259a6b7a4e59824bb1c215d9a8eee9286752bb9e88dce67dd6687146ea961a.png]

⇒ Population after 2ⁿd year = 62,500 × (80/100) = 50,000

**∴ The correct answer is 55000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by x% and then by y%, the net change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Multiplying Factor

To increase a value by r%, multiply by (1 + r/100). To decrease by r%, multiply by (1 − r/100).

Standard Population Formula

For a constant growth rate r, population after n years is Pₙ = P₀ × (1 + r/100)ⁿ.

questions.question: Lenses in spectacles help correct vision defects due to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Refraction of light through lenses**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vision defects occur when the light entering the eye does not focus exactly on the **Retina**. Spectacles correct this by using lenses that utilize the principle of **Refraction**.
 
• **Refraction** is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium (like air) into another (like glass or plastic lenses). By changing the path of light, the lens ensures that the image is formed precisely on the retina.
 
• In **Myopia** (nearsightedness), light focuses in front of the retina. A **Concave lens** (diverging lens) is used to spread the light rays slightly before they enter the eye, pushing the focus point back onto the retina.
 
• In **Hypermetropia** (farsightedness), light focuses behind the retina. A **Convex lens** (converging lens) is used to bend the light rays inward before they enter the eye, pulling the focus point forward onto the retina.
 
• **Dispersion** of light is the splitting of white light into its component colors (like in a prism), which is generally avoided in spectacle lenses to prevent colored fringes around objects.
 
• **Scattering** is the redirection of light in many directions by small particles, and **Reflection** is the bouncing of light off a surface (like a mirror), neither of which is the primary mechanism for correcting focus in spectacles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Power** of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length (in meters) and is measured in **Dioptres (D)**.
 
• **Presbyopia** is an age-related condition where the eye's natural lens loses flexibility, making it hard to focus on close objects; it is often corrected with **Bifocal** or **Progressive lenses**.
 
• **Astigmatism** occurs when the cornea or lens has an irregular shape, leading to blurred vision at all distances. It is corrected using **Cylindrical lenses**.
 
• The human eye contains a **Crystalline lens** which is a natural convex lens that forms a real and inverted image on the retina.

questions.question: Why does the palm feel cool when acetone is poured on it?

options.text: Particles remain still and reflect the surrounding heat.
Particles release energy to the palm and condense.
Particles absorb energy from the palm and evaporate.
Particles expand and trap air between skin layers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particles absorb energy from the palm and evaporate.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Acetone is a **volatile liquid**, which means it has a relatively low boiling point and converts into vapor easily at room temperature.
 
• The phenomenon responsible for the cooling sensation is **evaporation**. Evaporation is a **surface phenomenon** where liquid particles gain enough kinetic energy to escape into the gaseous phase.
 
• To transition from a liquid to a gas, the particles require energy known as the **latent heat of vaporization**.
 
• When acetone is poured on the palm, its particles **absorb this thermal energy** directly from the skin of the palm.
 
• Because the palm loses heat energy to the acetone, the temperature of the skin surface decreases, causing the person to feel a **cooling effect**.
 
• Other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• Particles in liquids are in **constant motion** and do not remain still.
 
• **Releasing energy** (exothermic process) would occur during condensation, which would make the palm feel warm, not cool.
 
• Expansion of particles trapping air is not the physical mechanism behind the cooling of volatile liquids.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acetone**, also known as **Propanone**, has the chemical formula CH₃COCH₃ . It is commonly used as a **nail polish remover**.
 
• The same principle applies to **perfumes**, **petrol**, and **rubbing alcohol** (isopropyl alcohol); they all feel cold on the skin due to rapid evaporation.
 
• **Evaporation causes cooling** is a fundamental principle used in **earthen pots (matkas)** to keep water cool and in the human body through **perspiration (sweating)** to maintain internal temperature.
 
• Factors that increase the rate of evaporation include **increased surface area**, **increased temperature**, **increased wind speed**, and **decreased humidity**.

questions.question: Which of the following officially determines the constitutional validity of any legislation?

options.text: The Parliament of India through a special resolution
The Union Cabinet through executive interpretation
The Supreme Court of India through judicial review
The President of India through constitutional discretion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Supreme Court of India through judicial review**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** is the final authority to determine the **constitutional validity** of any legislation or executive order through the doctrine of **Judicial Review**.
 
• **Judicial Review** is the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders of both the **Central and State governments**. If they are found to be violative of the **Constitution**, they can be declared as illegal, unconstitutional, and invalid.
 
• **Article 13** of the **Constitution of India** expressly provides for judicial review by declaring that all laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of the **Fundamental Rights** shall be void.
 
• The scope of judicial review in **India** is limited to three main aspects: **infringement of Fundamental Rights**, **lack of legislative competence** of the enacting body, and **contravention of constitutional provisions**.
 
• The **Supreme Court** and the **High Courts** derive their power of judicial review from several articles, including **Article 32** (Right to Constitutional Remedies) and **Article 226** (Power of High Courts to issue writs), respectively.
 
• In the landmark **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)**, the **Supreme Court** ruled that the power of **Judicial Review** is a **"basic feature"** of the **Constitution**, and therefore, it cannot be abrogated or even curtailed by a constitutional amendment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Parliament of India:**

 
 
• The **Parliament** is the supreme legislative body of **India**, consisting of the **President**, the **Rajya Sabha**, and the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• While **Parliament** has the power to enact and amend laws under **Article 368**, it cannot "officially determine" the validity of its own laws. Its legislative actions are always subject to the scrutiny of the courts to ensure they align with the **Constitutional** framework. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **The Union Cabinet:**
 
 
• The **Union Cabinet** is the core decision-making body of the **Executive**, headed by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• Its role is to formulate policies and aid in the execution of laws. While it interprets laws for administrative purposes, it does not have the judicial authority to declare a law constitutionally valid or invalid. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **The President of India:**
 
 
• The **President** is the **Head of State** and an integral part of **Parliament**. Under **Article 111**, the **President** gives assent to bills passed by **Parliament**.
 
• Under **Article 143** (Advisory Jurisdiction), the **President** can seek the opinion of the **Supreme Court** on a question of law or fact of public importance. However, the **President** does not have the discretion to "officially determine" validity; that remains a judicial function. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Origin of Judicial Review:** The concept of judicial review originated in the **USA** in the famous case of **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**, where Chief Justice **John Marshall** established the court's power to strike down laws.
 
• **Article 131-136:** These articles define the various jurisdictions of the **Supreme Court** (original, appellate, and special leave), which facilitate the process of reviewing the legality of governmental actions.
 
• **The 9th Schedule:** Initially intended to keep certain laws out of the reach of judicial review, the **Supreme Court** in the **I.R. Coelho case (2007)** ruled that laws placed in the **9th Schedule** after **April 24, 1973**, are open to challenge if they violate the **basic structure** of the **Constitution**.
 
• **Minerva Mills Case (1980):** The **Supreme Court** reiterated that a limited amending power of **Parliament** is itself a basic feature of the **Constitution**, and the court's power to review amendments is essential to maintain the **Supremacy of the Constitution**.

questions.question: Among five people named V, W, X, Y and Z, each have a certain age. X is twice the age of V. V is three times the age of Y. Y is one-fifth the age of W. The age of W is 15. If Z's age is equal the age of X, what is the age of Z?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Start from the known value: W = 15 years.

Calculate sequentially: Y = 15/5 = 3; V = 3 × 3 = 9; X = 2 × 9 = 18.

Given Z = X ⇒ Z = 18.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Age of W = 15

Age of Y = (1/5) × Age of W

Age of V = 3 × Age of Y

Age of X = 2 × Age of V

Age of Z = Age of X

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65e14394b8a9e1104aa9fc57ed4b2ba2a0c376707246d209db22ef4095132395.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Age of Y = 15 ÷ 5 = 3

⇒ Age of V = 3 × 3 = 9

⇒ Age of X = 9 × 2 = 18

⇒ Age of Z = Age of X = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Chains in Ages

When ages are given as multiples of each other, they form a ratio chain: X:V = 2:1, V:Y = 3:1, and Y:W = 1:5.

Effective Ratio Method

To find the direct relation between Z and W, multiply the ratios: Z/W = (Z/X) × (X/V) × (V/Y) × (Y/W) = 1 × 2 × 3 × (1/5) = 6/5. ∴ Z = 15 × (6/5) = 18.

Transitive Property of Equality

If Z = X and we calculate X = 18, then Z must be 18. This property is fundamental in solving logical comparison questions.

questions.question: Simplify: 125 ÷ 25 × 6 + 12 − 9
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve Division: 125 ÷ 25 = 5

Multiply result: 5 × 6 = 30

Perform Addition: 30 + 12 = 42

Subtract: 42 − 9 = 33

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 125 ÷ 25 × 6 + 12 − 9

**Formula:** Apply the BODMAS rule (Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction).

⇒ 125 ÷ 25 × 6 + 12 − 9

⇒ 5 × 6 + 12 − 9

⇒ 30 + 12 − 9

⇒ 42 − 9

⇒ 33

**∴ The correct answer is 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

V (Vinculum), B (Brackets), O (Of), D (Division), M (Multiplication), A (Addition), S (Subtraction).

Left-to-Right Priority

When operators of the same priority level like Division and Multiplication appear together, solve from left to right.

Subtraction of Larger Numbers

If the negative term is larger than the positive sum, the result will be negative: a − b = −(b − a) where b > a.

questions.question: A man buys a watch for ₹1,500. He sells it to his friend at a profit of 12% on his cost price. The friend then sells it to another person at a profit of 8% on his own cost price. What is the difference between the original cost price and the final selling price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive Profit % = x + y + (x × y)/100

Total Profit % = 12 + 8 + (12 × 8)/100 = 20 + 0.96 = 20.96%

Difference (Total Profit) = 20.96% of 1500

Difference = 1500 × 0.2096 = 15 × 20.96 = 314.40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹314.40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Original Cost Price (CP₁) = ₹1,500

First profit (p₁) = 12%

Second profit (p₂) = 8%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4367ce6a4ded5e9977373be5573f115176694ea13c3d1dc8dde31691117fa020.png] 

Formula used: Final SP = CP × (1 + p₁/100) × (1 + p₂/100)

⇒ Selling Price of Man (CP of Friend) = 1500 × (112/100)

⇒ Friend's CP = 15 × 112 = ₹1680

⇒ Final Selling Price = 1680 × (108/100)

⇒ Final SP = 16.8 × 108 = ₹1814.40

⇒ Difference = Final SP − Original CP

⇒ Difference = 1814.40 − 1500 = ₹314.40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹314.40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by x% and then by y%, the net change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Profit and Loss Relation

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (100 + Profit%)/100 or CP × (100 − Loss%)/100.

Effective Multiplier

For a profit of p%, the multiplier is (1 + p/100). For multiple transactions, multiply the individual factors.

questions.question: Which of the following hybridisation crossing is NOT used for the improvement in crop varieties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intraspecific**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hybridisation** refers to the crossing between genetically dissimilar plants to produce a new variety (hybrid) that possesses the combined desirable traits of both parents.
 
• In the context of **crop variety improvement**, hybridization is classified into three specific types based on the taxonomic relationship of the parents:
 
 
• **Intervarietal:** This involves crossing between two different **varieties** of the same species. It is the most common method used by plant breeders.
 
• **Interspecific:** This involves crossing between two different **species** belonging to the same **genus**. This is often used to transfer disease resistance from a wild species to a cultivated one.
 
• **Intergeneric:** This involves crossing between plants belonging to two different **genera**. Examples include **Triticale** (a cross between Wheat and Rye).
 
 
 
• **Intraspecific** crossing is a broad biological term meaning 'within the same species'. While **intervarietal** crossing is technically a form of intraspecific breeding, the term **Intraspecific** is not categorized as a distinct technique of crossing in the standard classification used for **crop improvement** methods (which focuses on the distinction between varieties, species, and genera).
 
• Therefore, among the given technical classifications, **Intraspecific** is the one not typically used as a designated category for improvement crossing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Apart from hybridization, crop improvement can also be achieved by **Genetic Manipulation**, where a specific **gene** is introduced to provide a desired characteristic, resulting in **Genetically Modified Crops (GMC)**.
 
• The primary objectives of these techniques include **Higher Yield**, **Improved Quality** (like protein quality in pulses or oil quality in oilseeds), **Biotic and Abiotic Resistance** (against pests, heat, or salinity), and **Wider Adaptability**.
 
• **Plant Breeding** also focuses on **Desirable Agronomic Characteristics**, such as tallness and profuse branching for fodder crops, or dwarfness for cereals to reduce nutrient consumption.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the effect of consuming ethanol?

options.text: Small amounts of dilute ethanol cause drunkenness, whereas absolute alcohol can be lethal
Long-term consumption of diluted ethanol has no health impact on humans
Absolute alcohol in any amount causes minor intoxication without severe effects
Small amounts of absolute alcohol are safe, but diluted ethanol is always fatal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Small amounts of dilute ethanol cause drunkenness, whereas absolute alcohol can be lethal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanol** (ethyl alcohol) is the active ingredient in all **alcoholic drinks**. In its **dilute form**, even small quantities can cause **drunkenness** or intoxication by acting as a **depressant** on the **central nervous system**.
 
• **Absolute alcohol** is nearly 100% pure ethanol. Unlike diluted alcohol, intake of even small quantities of absolute alcohol can be **lethal** because it is extremely concentrated and can cause sudden **respiratory failure** or severe metabolic shock.
 
• The statement that long-term consumption has no health impact is incorrect. Chronic intake of ethanol is linked to serious conditions such as **liver cirrhosis**, **cardiovascular diseases**, and **mental health disorders**.
 
• Consuming ethanol interferes with **metabolic processes** and slows down the reaction time of the brain, leading to a lack of **coordination** and **mental confusion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Methanol** (methyl alcohol) is far more dangerous than ethanol. When ingested, it is oxidized to **methanal** (formaldehyde) in the liver, which reacts with the **protoplasm** of cells, causing it to coagulate. It also attacks the **optic nerve**, which can lead to **permanent blindness**.
 
• To prevent the misuse of industrial alcohol for drinking, it is often **denatured** by adding poisonous substances like methanol or dyes like **copper sulphate** to give it a blue color. This is known as **denatured alcohol**.
 
• **Ethanol** is widely used as a **solvent** in the pharmaceutical industry for making medicines like **tincture of iodine**, cough syrups, and various tonics.
 
• In some countries, alcohol is used as an additive in **petrol** (gasoline) to create a cleaner fuel known as **gasohol**, as ethanol burns to produce only carbon dioxide and water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The problem describes a car in **free fall** under the influence of gravity. In such cases, the car starts from a state of rest as it falls off the ledge.
 
• The **initial velocity (u)** is 0 m/s.
 
• The **acceleration (a)** acting on the car is the **acceleration due to gravity (g)**, which is given as 10 m/s².
 
• The **time (t)** taken to reach the ground is 0.8 s.
 
• To calculate the **height (h)** or distance (s), we use the **second equation of motion**:

 s = ut + (1)/(2)at² 
 
• Substituting the known values into the equation:
 
 
• h = (0 × 0.8) + (1/2 × 10 × (0.8)²)
 
• h = 0 + (5 × 0.64)
 
• h = **3.2 m**
 
 
 
• Thus, the ledge is **3.2 meters** above the ground.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• First equation: v = u + at
 
• Second equation: s = ut + 1/2 at²

questions.question: No matter where an object is placed in front of it, a concave lens always forms an image that is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual, erect, and diminished**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave lens** is a lens that possesses at least one surface that curves inwards. It is thinner at the center than at the edges.
 
• It is also known as a **diverging lens** because it spreads out the light rays that have been refracted through it.
 
• No matter where the object is placed (whether at infinity or between infinity and the optical center), a concave lens always forms an image that is **virtual**, **erect**, and **diminished**.
 
• A **virtual image** is formed because the diverging rays do not actually meet; they only appear to meet when produced backwards. Therefore, the image cannot be obtained on a **screen**.
 
• The image is always located on the same side of the lens as the object, specifically between the **optical center (O)** and the **principal focus (F)**.
 
• The size of the image is always **smaller** than the size of the object, which is why it is termed **diminished**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Lens Formula** is given by (1)/(f) = (1)/(v) - (1)/(u) , where **f** is the focal length, **v** is the image distance, and **u** is the object distance.
 
• For a concave lens, the **focal length (f)** is always taken as **negative** according to the sign convention.
 
• **Magnification (m)** for a lens is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, expressed as m = (v)/(u) . Since the image formed by a concave lens is always smaller than the object and erect, its magnification is always **positive** and **less than 1**.
 
• Concave lenses are commonly used in **eyeglasses** to correct **myopia** (nearsightedness), in **flashlights** to spread light, and in **peepholes** of doors.

questions.question: An article is sold at a profit of 40%. If the cost price is increased by ₹28 and the selling price is reduced by ₹84, then the profit would be 37.5%. What is the original cost price (in ₹) of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio (CP : SP) = 100 : 140 = 5 : 7

New Ratio (CP : SP) = 8 : 11 (Profit = 37.5% = 3/8)

Cross Multiplication: (5 × 11 − 8 × 7) units = 8 × (−84) − 11 × 28

−1 unit = −672 − 308 ⇒ 1 unit = 980

Original CP = 5 units = 5 × 980 = 4900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial profit = 40%, New profit = 37.5%, Change in CP = +₹28, Change in SP = −₹84.

**Formula Used:** SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4428bd7dd20c909069a9602fead266c5842058f31666a17d64ba0ffb925f1907.png] 

⇒ Let original CP = 100x and SP = 140x

⇒ New CP = 100x + 28

⇒ New SP = 140x − 84

⇒ New SP = New CP × (1 + 37.5/100) = New CP × (1 + 3/8)

⇒ 140x − 84 = (100x + 28) × 11/8

⇒ 8 × (140x − 84) = 11 × (100x + 28)

⇒ 1120x − 672 = 1100x + 308

⇒ 1120x − 1100x = 308 + 672

⇒ 20x = 980

⇒ Original CP = 100x = 5 × (20x) = 5 × 980 = 4900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 | Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.

Fractional Conversion of Percentages

Standard values like 37.5% = 3/8, 12.5% = 1/8, and 62.5% = 5/8 are used to convert ratio calculations into simple integer steps.

Relation between CP and SP

SP = CP × [(100 + P%)/100] when there is a profit, and SP = CP × [(100 − L%)/100] when there is a loss.
